text.p: Orbital Sciences Corp said on Wednesday that NASA's launch of the Pegasus XL was halted at 1241 EST when a locking pin on the rocket's rudder failed to properly disengage.
The Pegasus XL, a scientific spacecraft, commenced the launch at 1149 EST, when the L-1011 carrier aircraft took off from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility, Orbital Sciences said.
When the locking pin failed to work properly, the L-1011 aircraft safely returned the Pegasus vehicle and the attached satellites to Wallops.
Orbital stated that until this problem surfaced just prior to the scheduled launch time, all Pegasus systems were performing as designed, the company said.
The exact date for a second launch attempt will be set once final analysis of the problem is complete, but the delay will be at least several days, Orbital said.
